---
title: "3 · Library and design matrix"
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
source("R/page_setup.R")
wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")
traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")
```

## Drivers

The drivers $u_1, \dots, u_4$ (`TT`, `DL`, `RAW`, `RAD`) are standardised to mean 0 and standard deviation 1. The response does not enter this step.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_drivers")
```

```{r}
drv <- make_drivers(wx)
dim(drv$U)            # season x day x driver
```

## Library

The library contains powers of each driver up to degree 3, giving $K = 12$ terms; the constant term is the intercept of the regression.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("library_matrix", "make_library")
```

```{r}
Theta <- make_library(drv)
dim(Theta)            # season x day x term
dimnames(Theta)[[3]]
```

## Response

The biomass trajectories are stored in an array `Y[genotype, season, day]` with `NA` after maturity.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_trajectories")
```

```{r}
tr <- make_trajectories(traj, drv)
dim(tr$Y)
```

## Design matrix

For one genotype, the rows of $\mathbf{X}$ are the days of all seasons and the columns are the library terms; $\Delta\mathbf{y}$ holds the daily biomass increments $y_{i+1} - y_i$.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("make_design")
```

```{r}
d <- make_design(Theta, tr, "g001")
dim(d$X)
round(head(d$X, 3), 2)
head(d$dy)
```

The regression of the increments on the library is a linear model:

```{r}
round(coef(lm(d$dy ~ d$X)), 3)
```

Step 4 replaces `lm` by other methods.
